title.zh: 卷一百九十三 列傳第八十: 忠義一
title.en: Volume 193 Biographies 80: Loyal and Righteous Acts 1
title.raw: 卷一百九十三 列傳第八十: 忠義一 Volume 193 Biographies 80: Loyal and Righteous Acts 1

sentences.zh: 李伯溫，守賢之孫，彀之子也。

translations.literal: Li Bowen was the grandson of Shouxian and the son of Gou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bowen was a grandson of Shouxian and a son of Gou.

sentences.zh: 長兄惟則，懷遠大將軍、平陽征行萬戶；

translations.literal: His elder brother Weize was Grand General of Huaiyuan and campaigning commander of ten thousand households at Pingyang;
translations.idiomatic: His eldest brother, Weize, held the titles Grand General of Huaiyuan and campaigning commander of ten thousand households at Pingyang;

sentences.zh: 次伯通。

translations.literal: Next was Botong.
translations.idiomatic: The next brother was Botong.

sentences.zh: 歲甲戌，錦州張致叛，國王木華黎命擊之，大戰城北，伯通死焉。

translations.literal: In the year jiaxu, Zhang Zhi of Jinzhou rebelled; Prince Muqali ordered an attack; a great battle was fought north of the city, and Botong died there.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiaxu year, Zhang Zhi of Jinzhou rose in rebellion. Prince Muqali ordered an assault; a fierce battle was fought north of the city wall, and Botong fell there.

sentences.zh: 伯溫行平陽元帥府事，鎮青龍堡，專任東征。

translations.literal: Bowen acted as chief of the Pingyang Marshal's Office, garrisoned Qinglong Fort, and was solely charged with the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Bowen administered the Pingyang Marshal's Office, held Qinglong Fort, and bore sole responsibility for operations in the east.

sentences.zh: 知平陽已陷，弟守忠被執，選驍勇拒守，久之，金人盡銳來攻，守卒夜多遁去，李成開水門導敵入，伯溫登堞樓，謂左右曰：「吾兄弟仗節擁麾，受方面之寄，今不幸失利，當以死報國。

translations.literal: Learning that Pingyang had fallen and that his younger brother Shouzhong had been captured, he selected the bravest troops to hold out in defense. After a long time the Jin brought their full strength to attack; many defenders fled by night; Li Cheng opened the water gate to admit the enemy. Bowen ascended the parapet tower and said to those beside him: "We brothers, bearing our standards in loyalty, were entrusted with a regional command. Now that we have met with misfortune and defeat, we must repay the state with our lives.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Pingyang had fallen and his younger brother Shouzhong had been taken, he chose the fiercest troops to resist. After a long siege the Jin attacked with their full strength; many defenders slipped away in the night, and Li Cheng opened the water gate to let the enemy in. Bowen climbed the parapet tower and told those around him: "We brothers have upheld our banners in loyalty and were entrusted with a whole region. Now that fortune has turned against us, we must repay the state with our deaths.

sentences.zh: 吾弟已被執，我不可再辱，汝等宜自逃生。

translations.literal: My younger brother has already been captured; I cannot suffer disgrace again. You should make your own escape.
translations.idiomatic: My brother is already a prisoner; I cannot endure dishonor a second time. You should save yourselves and flee.

sentences.zh: 」士卒皆猶豫不忍去，伯溫即拔劍殺家屬，投井中，以刃植柱，刺心而死。

translations.literal: The soldiers all hesitated and were unwilling to leave; Bowen at once drew his sword and killed his household, threw them into a well, planted his blade in a pillar, and stabbed himself through the heart to die.
translations.idiomatic: The troops hung back, unwilling to abandon him. Bowen drew his sword, slew his family, cast their bodies into a well, set his blade upright against a pillar, and drove it through his own heart.

sentences.zh: 金人登樓，見伯溫抱柱如生，無不嗟歎。

translations.literal: When the Jin troops mounted the tower they saw Bowen embracing the pillar as if alive; none failed to sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin climbed the tower and saw Bowen still clasping the pillar as though he lived, every man sighed in wonder.

sentences.zh: 子守正，自幼時嘗質於木華黎，後為平陽守，活俘虜甚衆，以功授銀青榮祿大夫、河東南路兵馬都元帥。

translations.literal: His son Shouzheng, from childhood had been held as a hostage with Muqali; later he became defender of Pingyang, spared many captives alive, and for his merit was appointed Silver-Green Glory and Blessings Grand Master and commander-in-chief of military forces on the Southern Hedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouzheng had been sent as a hostage to Muqali in his youth. He later served as defender of Pingyang, spared a great many prisoners, and for these services was made Silver-Green Glory and Blessings Grand Master and commander-in-chief of the Southern Hedong Circuit forces.

sentences.zh: 歲庚寅，上黨、晉陽合兵攻汾州，將陷，守正以義赴援，衆寡不敵，別遣老弱百人，曳薪揚塵，多張旗幟，敵懼，遂解去。

translations.literal: In the year gengyin, Shangdang and Jinyang combined forces to attack Fenzhou, which was on the verge of falling. Shouzheng went to its aid out of righteousness; his numbers were too few to match the enemy. He separately sent out a hundred old and weak men to drag firewood and raise dust, and set up many banners and flags; the enemy grew afraid and thereupon lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengyin year, Shangdang and Jinyang joined forces against Fenzhou, which was near collapse. Shouzheng marched to its relief on principle, but he was heavily outnumbered. He detached a hundred aged and infirm men to drag brushwood and kick up dust, while he raised a forest of banners. The enemy took fright and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 汾人持牛酒迎犒者，道不絕，且泣謝曰：「幸公完是州，德甚大，願奉是州以從。

translations.literal: The people of Fen bore cattle and wine to welcome and reward him along the road without cease, and weeping thanked him, saying: "Fortunately you preserved this prefecture; your virtue is very great. We wish to offer this prefecture to follow you.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Fen lined the road with cattle and wine to welcome him, weeping as they thanked him: "You have saved our prefecture; your kindness is beyond measure. We would gladly submit this prefecture to your command."

sentences.zh: 」關中兵屯吉州，酋領楊鐵槍以數千人叛，守正出兵擒之。

translations.literal: Guanzhong troops were stationed at Jizhou; the chieftain Yang Tieqiang rebelled with several thousand men, and Shouzheng led troops out and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong forces were encamped at Jizhou when the chieftain Yang Tieqiang revolted with several thousand men. Shouzheng marched out and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 軒成據隰州，守正往擊之，中矢傷足，及歸，瘡甚，會金人完顏合達攻平陽，守正裹瘡戰歿。

translations.literal: Xuan Cheng held Xizhou; Shouzheng went to attack him, was struck by an arrow and wounded in the foot; when he returned the wound grew severe. It happened that the Jin commander Wanyan Hedai attacked Pingyang; Shouzheng, binding his wound, fought and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Cheng held Xizhou, and Shouzheng went to strike him. An arrow struck his foot; by the time he returned, the wound had grown grave. Just then the Jin general Wanyan Hedai assaulted Pingyang. Shouzheng bound his wound and fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 大帥以其兄守忠代之。

translations.literal: The supreme commander replaced him with his elder brother Shouzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The supreme commander appointed his elder brother Shouzhong in his place.

sentences.zh: 守忠官至銀青榮祿大夫、河東南路兵馬都元帥，兼知平陽府事。

translations.literal: Shouzhong reached the office of Silver-Green Glory and Blessings Grand Master and commander-in-chief of military forces on the Southern Hedong Circuit, and concurrently administered the affairs of Pingyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong rose to Silver-Green Glory and Blessings Grand Master and commander-in-chief of the Southern Hedong Circuit forces, while also serving as administrator of Pingyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 壬午冬，平陽公胡景山以青龍堡降。

translations.literal: In the winter of the renwu year, Duke Hu Jingshan of Pingyang surrendered Qinglong Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the renwu year, Duke Hu Jingshan of Pingyang surrendered Qinglong Fort to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 嘗從攻益都，北還，軍將彭智孫，乘間據義州叛，守忠聞之，長驅抵城下，力戰，復之。

translations.literal: He had once followed in the attack on Yidu; on the return north, the army officer Peng Zhisun seized an opportunity to hold Yizhou in rebellion. When Shouzhong heard of it he drove straight to the city, fought fiercely, and recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: He had once joined the assault on Yidu. On the march back north, the officer Peng Zhisun seized his chance and seized Yizhou in revolt. Shouzhong heard the news, rode hard to the walls, fought fiercely, and retook the city.

sentences.zh: 丁亥夏四月，金紇石烈真襲擊平陽行營招討使權國王按察兒於洪洞，守忠出援之，會於高梁，師潰入城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the dinghai year, the Jin commander He Shiliezhen raided the Pingyang campaign pacification commissioner and acting prince Aichar at Hongtong. Shouzhong went out to reinforce him; they met at Gaoliang; the army was routed and fled into the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer in the dinghai year, the Jin commander He Shiliezhen raided the Pingyang campaign pacification commissioner and acting prince Aichar at Hongtong. Shouzhong marched to his aid; they met at Gaoliang, but their forces broke and poured back into the city.

sentences.zh: 平陽副帥夾谷常德潛獻東門以納金兵，城遂陷。

translations.literal: The deputy commander of Pingyang, Jiagu Changde, secretly offered the eastern gate to admit Jin troops, and the city thereupon fell.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy commander of Pingyang, Jiagu Changde, secretly opened the eastern gate to the Jin, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 金人執守忠至汴，誘以高爵，使降，守忠罵之，語惡，金人怒，置守忠鐵籠中，火炙死。

translations.literal: The Jin seized Shouzhong and brought him to Bian; they tempted him with high rank and urged him to surrender. Shouzhong cursed them with vile words; the Jin grew angry, placed Shouzhong in an iron cage, and roasted him to death with fire.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin took Shouzhong to Bian and tempted him with lofty rank to make him submit. He cursed them in the foulest terms. Enraged, they shut him in an iron cage and burned him alive.

sentences.zh: 石珪，泰安新泰人，宋徂徠先生守道之裔孫也，世以讀書力田為業。

translations.literal: Shi Gui was a man of Xintai in Tai'an, a descendant of the Song scholar Shoudao of Mount Culai, whose family for generations took reading and farming as their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Gui came from Xintai in Tai'an. He was a descendant of the Song scholar Shoudao of Mount Culai, and his family for generations had lived by study and tillage.

sentences.zh: 體貌魁偉，膂力過人，倜儻不羈。

translations.literal: His physique was imposing, his strength surpassed other men, and he was bold and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and powerfully built, stronger than ordinary men, and free-spirited by nature.

sentences.zh: 金貞祐南渡，兵戈四起，珪率少壯，負險自保，與滕陽陳敬宗聚兵山東，破張都統、李霸王兵於龜蒙山。

translations.literal: When the Jin moved south under the Zhenyou reign, warfare broke out on all sides. Gui led the young and strong to hold perilous ground and defend themselves, joined Chen Jingzong of Tengyang to gather troops in Shandong, and defeated the forces of Commander Zhang and Overlord Li at Mount Guimeng.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin court fled south in the Zhenyou era and war spread everywhere, Gui rallied the young men of his district to hold the high ground and defend themselves. He joined Chen Jingzong of Tengyang in raising forces across Shandong and routed the armies of Commander Zhang and Overlord Li at Mount Guimeng.

sentences.zh: 宋將鄭元龍以兵迎敵，珪敗之於亳陽，遂乘勝引兵入盱眙。

translations.literal: The Song general Zheng Yuanlong came with troops to meet the enemy; Gui defeated him at Haoyang and thereupon, pressing the advantage, led his army into Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song general Zheng Yuanlong marched out to oppose him, Gui defeated him at Haoyang and, riding the momentum, drove his army into Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 會宋賈涉誘殺漣水忠義軍統轄季先，人情不安，衆迎珪為帥，呼為太尉。

translations.literal: It happened that the Song official Jia She lured and killed Ji Xian, commander of the Loyal and Righteous Army at Lianshui; popular feeling was unsettled, and the masses welcomed Gui as commander, calling him Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Song minister Jia She had treacherously killed Ji Xian, commander of the Loyal and Righteous Army at Lianshui, and morale was shaken. The people acclaimed Gui as their leader and addressed him as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 歲戊寅，太祖使葛葛不罕與宋議和。

translations.literal: In the year wuyin, the Founder sent Gegu Buhan to negotiate peace with the Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuyin year, the Founder dispatched Gegu Buhan to treat for peace with the Song.

sentences.zh: 己卯，珪令麾下劉順直抵尋斯干城，入覲，太祖慰勞順，且敕珪曰：「如宋和議不成，吾與爾永結一家，吾必榮汝。

translations.literal: In the year jimao, Gui ordered his subordinate Liu Shun to go straight to the city of Xingsigan to have an audience. The Founder comforted and rewarded Shun, and moreover instructed Gui: "If the Song peace talks do not succeed, I and you shall be bound as one family forever; I shall surely honor you.
translations.idiomatic: In the jimao year, Gui sent his lieutenant Liu Shun straight to the court at Xingsigan for an audience. The Founder received Shun warmly and sent word to Gui: "If peace with the Song fails, you and I shall be one household forever, and I shall surely exalt you."

sentences.zh: 」順還告珪，珪心感服，日夜思降。

translations.literal: Shun returned and reported to Gui; Gui's heart was moved to submission, and day and night he thought of surrendering.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun returned and told him this, Gui was deeply moved and from that day thought constantly of submitting.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，宋果渝盟，珪棄其妻孔氏、子金山，杖劍渡淮，宋將追之曰：「太尉迴，完汝妻子。

translations.literal: In the year gengchen the Song indeed broke the treaty. Gui abandoned his wife Lady Kong and son Jinshan, took sword in hand and crossed the Huai. A Song general pursued him, calling: "Grand Marshal, turn back and we will restore your wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengchen year the Song duly broke the treaty. Gui left behind his wife Lady Kong and his son Jinshan, drew his sword, and crossed the Huai. A Song officer pursued him, shouting: "Grand Marshal, turn back and your family will be spared."

sentences.zh: 」珪不顧，宋將沉珪妻子於淮。

translations.literal: Gui paid no heed; the Song general drowned Gui's wife and son in the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Gui did not look back. The Song officer had his wife and son drowned in the Huai.

sentences.zh: 遂率順及李溫，因孛里海歸木華黎。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led Shun and Li Wen, and through Bolihai returned to Muqali.
translations.idiomatic: He then led Shun and Li Wen back through Bolihai to join Muqali.

sentences.zh: 木華黎悅之，謂曰：「若得東平、南京，授汝判之。」

translations.literal: Muqali was pleased with him and said: "If we take Dongping and Nanjing, I shall appoint you to govern them."
translations.idiomatic: Muqali received him gladly and said: "When we take Dongping and Nanjing, I shall put you in charge of them."

sentences.zh: 辛巳，木華黎承制授珪光祿大夫、濟兗單三州兵馬都緫管、山東路行元帥，佩金虎符，便宜從事。

translations.literal: In the year xinsi, Muqali, acting by imperial commission, appointed Gui Glory and Blessings Grand Master, overall commander of military forces in the three prefectures of Ji, Yan, and Shan, and campaigning marshal of the Shandong Circuit, with a golden tiger tally and discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinsi year Muqali, acting under imperial commission, made Gui Glory and Blessings Grand Master, overall commander of the Ji, Yan, and Shan prefectures, and campaigning marshal of the Shandong Circuit, granting him a golden tiger tally and full discretionary power.

sentences.zh: 後金棄東平，珪與嚴實分據，收輯濟、兗、沂、滕、單諸州。

translations.literal: Later the Jin abandoned Dongping; Gui and Yan Shi divided the territory between them and gathered in the prefectures of Ji, Yan, Yi, Teng, and Shan.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin abandoned Dongping, Gui and Yan Shi divided the region between them and brought the prefectures of Ji, Yan, Yi, Teng, and Shan back under control.

sentences.zh: 癸未，太祖詔曰：「石珪棄妻子，提兵歸順，戰勝攻取，加授金紫光祿大夫、東平兵馬都緫管、山東諸路都元帥，餘如故。」

translations.literal: In the year guiwei, the Founder issued an edict: "Shi Gui abandoned wife and children, led troops in submission, and in battle conquered and seized. He is further appointed Golden Purple Glory and Blessings Grand Master, overall commander of military forces at Dongping, and supreme marshal of all circuits in Shandong; the rest as before."
translations.idiomatic: In the guiwei year the Founder decreed: "Shi Gui left wife and child behind, brought his troops in submission, and has fought with repeated success. He is further promoted to Golden Purple Glory and Blessings Grand Master, overall commander of Dongping forces, and supreme marshal of all Shandong circuits; his other offices remain unchanged."

sentences.zh: 秋七月，珪領兵破曹州，與金將鄭從宜連戰數晝夜，糧絕，援兵不至，軍無叛意，珪臨陣馬仆被擒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, Gui led troops to storm Caozhou and fought the Jin general Zheng Congyi for several days and nights in succession. Provisions ran out and reinforcements did not arrive; the army showed no intent to rebel. Gui, on the battlefield, had his horse fall and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Gui led an assault on Caozhou and battled the Jin general Zheng Congyi for days on end. Supplies ran out and no reinforcements came, yet his men would not turn traitor. In the thick of the fight his horse stumbled and he was taken.

sentences.zh: 囚至汴，金主壯其為人，誘以名爵，欲使揖，珪憤然曰：「吾身事大朝，官至光祿，復能受封他國耶！

translations.literal: Imprisoned and brought to Bian, the Jin ruler admired his character and tempted him with titles and offices, wishing to make him bow. Gui said in anger: "My person serves the Great Dynasty and I have reached the rank of Glory and Blessings Grand Master—how could I again accept enfeoffment from another state!
translations.idiomatic: Taken in chains to Bian, the Jin emperor admired his bearing and tempted him with rank and titles, demanding a bow of submission. Gui flared up and said: "I serve the Great Dynasty and have risen to Glory and Blessings Grand Master—how could I accept honors from another realm!"

sentences.zh: 假我一朝，當縛爾以獻。

translations.literal: Give me but one morning and I shall bind you and present you as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Give me but a single morning and I will bind you and deliver you up as my offering.

sentences.zh: 」金主大怒，蒸殺于市，珪怡然就死，色不變。

translations.literal: The Jin ruler was greatly enraged and had him steamed to death in the marketplace. Gui went to his death calmly, his countenance unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor flew into a rage and had him steamed alive in the marketplace. Gui went to his death serene, his face unaltered.

sentences.zh: 其麾下立社兗州祀焉。

translations.literal: His followers established a shrine at Yanzhou to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: His followers founded a shrine at Yanzhou in his honor.

sentences.zh: 攸哈剌拔都，渤海人。

translations.literal: You Halabatu was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: You Halabatu came from Bohai.

sentences.zh: 初名興哥，世農家，善射，以武斷鄉井。

translations.literal: His original name was Xingge; his family for generations were farmers; he was skilled at archery and ruled the countryside by force of arms.
translations.idiomatic: Originally named Xingge, he came from a farming family, excelled at archery, and dominated his district by force.

sentences.zh: 金末，避地大寧。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jin he fled to take refuge in Daning.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Jin dynasty he fled to Daning for safety.

sentences.zh: 國兵至，出保高州富庶寨，射獵以食。

translations.literal: When the state's army arrived, he went out to hold the Fushu Stockade at Gaozhou and hunted for food.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial armies arrived, he withdrew to hold the Fushu Stockade in Gaozhou and lived by hunting.

sentences.zh: 屢奪大營孳畜，又射死其追者。

translations.literal: He repeatedly seized livestock from the great camp and also shot dead those who pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he raided the main camp for livestock and shot down those sent in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 國王木華黎率兵攻寨，寨破，奔高州，國兵圍城，下令曰：「能斬攸興哥首以降，則城中居民皆獲生。

translations.literal: Prince Muqali led troops to attack the stockade; when the stockade fell he fled to Gaozhou. The state's army besieged the city and issued an order: "Whoever can cut off You Xingge's head and surrender—the city's inhabitants shall all be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Muqali attacked the stockade; when it fell, Xingge fled to Gaozhou. The imperial forces besieged the city and proclaimed: "Whoever brings You Xingge's head in surrender shall save every soul within these walls."

sentences.zh: 」守者召謂曰：「汝奇男子，吾寧忍斷汝首以獻，汝其往降乎！

translations.literal: The defenders summoned him and said: "You are a remarkable man; how could we bear to cut off your head and present it? Will you not go and surrender!
translations.idiomatic: The defenders called him in and said: "You are a man of rare mettle—we could never bring ourselves to take your head. Go and surrender!"

sentences.zh: 不然，吾一城生靈，無噍類矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise not a single living soul in our whole city will remain.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise not one living soul in this city will be left."

sentences.zh: 」興哥乃折矢出降。

translations.literal: Xingge thereupon broke an arrow and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xingge broke an arrow in token of submission and came out to yield.

sentences.zh: 諸將怒，欲殺之，木華黎曰：「壯士也，留之為吾用。

translations.literal: The generals were angry and wished to kill him. Muqali said: "A brave man—keep him for my use.
translations.idiomatic: The generals were furious and wanted him killed, but Muqali said: "This is a true warrior—keep him and put him to work for me."

sentences.zh: 」俾隸麾下。

translations.literal: He was made to serve under his command.
translations.idiomatic: He was placed in Muqali's own retinue.

sentences.zh: 從木華黎攻通州，獻計，一夕造砲三十、雲梯數十，附城，州將懼，出寶貨以降。

translations.literal: Following Muqali in the attack on Tongzhou, he offered a plan: in one night they built thirty cannon and several tens of scaling ladders, pressed them to the wall, and the prefectural commander grew afraid and came out with treasures to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In Muqali's assault on Tongzhou he proposed a plan: in a single night they built thirty cannon and dozens of scaling ladders and pressed them against the walls. The prefectural commander took fright and surrendered his treasure.

sentences.zh: 木華黎命興哥恣取之，興哥獨取良馬三，以賞兵士。

translations.literal: Muqali ordered Xingge to take whatever he pleased; Xingge took only three fine horses and used them to reward the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali told him to take whatever he wished; Xingge chose only three fine horses and gave them to his men as rewards.

sentences.zh: 木華黎以其功聞太祖，賜名哈剌拔都。

translations.literal: Muqali reported his merit to the Founder, who bestowed on him the name Halabatu.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali reported his deeds to the Founder, who granted him the name Halabatu.

sentences.zh: 從木華黎略地燕南，為先鋒，至大名，金將徒單登城督戰，哈剌拔都射之，中左目，其部將開門南奔，追殺將盡。

translations.literal: Following Muqali in reducing the lands south of Yan, he served as vanguard. At Daming the Jin general Tudan mounted the wall to direct the battle; Halabatu shot him and struck his left eye. His subordinate officers opened the gate and fled south; they were pursued and nearly all slain.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Muqali through the lands south of Yan as vanguard. At Daming the Jin general Tudan stood on the wall directing the fight; Halabatu shot him through the left eye. The officers flung open the southern gate and fled; the pursuers cut down nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 論功，賜金符，充隨營監察。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed he was given a golden tally and appointed camp inspector attached to the army.
translations.idiomatic: For his services he received a golden tally and was made inspector attached to the field army.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，授金虎符、龍虎衛上將軍、河東北路兵馬都元帥，鎮太原。

translations.literal: In the year wuyin he was given a golden tiger tally, made General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, and appointed commander-in-chief of military forces on the Northern Hedong Circuit, garrisoning Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuyin year he received a golden tiger tally, was made General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, and was appointed commander-in-chief of the Northern Hedong Circuit forces, with Taiyuan as his seat.

sentences.zh: 時太原新破，哈剌拔都修城池，繕兵甲，招降屬邑，市肆不改，遠近聞之，皆相率來歸。

translations.literal: At that time Taiyuan had newly been taken; Halabatu repaired the walls and moats, put arms and armor in order, received the surrender of subordinate districts, and left the markets unchanged. When those far and near heard of it they all came in groups to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan had only just fallen when Halabatu set about repairing the walls, rearming his troops, and accepting the submission of outlying districts without disturbing the markets. Word spread, and people came in from far and near to submit.

sentences.zh: 嘗微服夜出，聞民間語曰：「吾屬父母子女相失矣，死者不可復生，生者無以為贖，奈何！

translations.literal: Once he went out at night in plain dress and heard people in the streets say: "Our parents, children, and spouses have been separated from us; the dead cannot be brought back to life, and the living have no means to ransom them—what is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: One night he went out in disguise and overheard people saying: "Our parents, children, and spouses have been torn apart; the dead cannot return, and the living have no way to ransom them—what can we do?"

sentences.zh: 」明日，下令軍中，凡俘獲有親者聽贖，無貲者官為贖之，民得完聚者衆。

translations.literal: The next day he issued an order in the army: all captives who had kin were permitted to be ransomed; those without means the government would ransom for them. Many among the people were able to be reunited whole.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he ordered that any captive with kin might be redeemed, and that those without means would be redeemed at public expense. A great many families were reunited.

sentences.zh: 庚辰二月，金梁知府立西風寨，奪居民耕牛，民群訴之，哈剌拔都領數騎，追殺梁知府，梟首西門，驅耕牛還。

translations.literal: In the second month of the gengchen year, the Jin prefect Liang established Xifeng Stockade and seized the people's plow oxen. The people appealed in a body; Halabatu led a few horsemen, pursued and killed Prefect Liang, displayed his head at the western gate, and drove the plow oxen back.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the gengchen year the Jin prefect Liang set up Xifeng Stockade and seized the peasants' oxen. When the people petitioned en masse, Halabatu rode out with a handful of men, ran down Prefect Liang and killed him, hung his head at the western gate, and returned the oxen to their owners.

sentences.zh: 木華黎由葭州渡河西行，哈剌拔都迎之，道破隰州及懸窯、地洞諸寨。

translations.literal: Muqali crossed west of the river from Jiazhou; Halabatu went to meet him and along the way stormed Xizhou and the stockades of Xuanyao, Didong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Muqali crossed the river westward from Jiazhou, Halabatu went to meet him and on the way reduced Xizhou and the stockades at Xuanyao, Didong, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 辛巳三月，金兵攻壽陽縣王胡莊，垂破，時左右裨將各分兵守險，城中見卒不滿百，哈剌拔都夜半引甲騎十餘人救之，道三交，見金兵舉烽東、西兩山，哈剌拔都趨之，大戰。

translations.literal: In the third month of the xinsi year, Jin troops attacked Wanghu Stockade in Shouyang County, which was on the verge of falling. At that time the left and right deputy generals had each divided their forces to hold perilous ground; the visible troops in the city were fewer than a hundred. Halabatu at midnight led a dozen or so armored horsemen to its relief. On the road at Sanjiao he saw Jin troops raising beacon fires on the eastern and western hills; Halabatu rushed toward them and fought a great battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the xinsi year Jin forces assaulted Wanghu Stockade in Shouyang County, which was near collapse. His deputy commanders had split their men to hold the passes, and fewer than a hundred troops remained visible in the city. At midnight Halabatu led a dozen armored horsemen to the rescue. At Sanjiao he saw Jin beacon fires on the eastern and western hills and charged into a fierce battle.

sentences.zh: 天將明，金兵遁去，擣太原之虛，由西門俘獲哈剌拔都家屬。

translations.literal: As dawn approached the Jin troops fled. They feigned an attack on Taiyuan and through the western gate seized Halabatu's household.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the Jin withdrew, then feinted against Taiyuan and swept in through the western gate to seize Halabatu's family.

sentences.zh: 哈剌拔都聞之，徑趨西山，復奪以還。

translations.literal: When Halabatu heard of it he went straight to the western hills and recovered them by force.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, he rode straight for the western hills and fought his way to bring them back.

sentences.zh: 五月，金趙權府率兵三萬圍太原，哈剌拔都將騎三十，出西門，令騎曳柴揚塵，聲言曰：「國兵三萬至矣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Jin commander Zhao Quanfu led thirty thousand troops to besiege Taiyuan. Halabatu led thirty horsemen out the western gate, ordered the riders to drag brushwood and raise dust, and proclaimed aloud: "The state's army of thirty thousand has arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Jin commander Zhao Quanfu brought thirty thousand men to besiege Taiyuan. Halabatu led thirty horsemen out the western gate, had them drag brushwood to raise dust, and shouted: "Thirty thousand imperial troops have arrived!"

sentences.zh: 」金兵懼，潰去。

translations.literal: The Jin troops grew afraid and broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin panicked and broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 癸未，金馬武京來攻太谷縣桑梓寨，哈剌拔都設伏于險，將輕騎衝其陣，伏發，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the year guiwei, the Jin commander Ma Wujing came to attack Sangzi Stockade in Taigu County. Halabatu set an ambush in a perilous place, led light cavalry to charge their formation, and when the ambush sprang they were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the guiwei year the Jin commander Ma Wujing attacked Sangzi Stockade in Taigu County. Halabatu laid an ambush in difficult terrain, led light cavalry in a headlong charge, and when his hidden troops sprang up routed the enemy completely.

sentences.zh: 時太原諸邑皆平，唯石家昂及盂州陵井寨、忻州清泉寨為唇齒，皆未下。

translations.literal: At that time all districts around Taiyuan were pacified; only Shijia'ang and Lingjing Stockade in Mengzhou and Qingquan Stockade in Xinzhou, mutually supporting like lips and teeth, had not yet fallen.
translations.idiomatic: By then every district around Taiyuan had submitted; only Shijia'ang, Lingjing Stockade in Mengzhou, and Qingquan Stockade in Xinzhou still held together like interlocking defenses, and none had yet fallen.

sentences.zh: 甲申十月，將兵至陵井，遣卒叩寨門，詐曰納糧芻，守者弗悟，門啟，徑入，蹂踐之，衆潰，其酋長走石家昂，遂平陵井寨。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the jiashen year he led troops to Lingjing, sent soldiers to knock at the stockade gate and falsely say they were delivering grain and fodder. The defenders did not perceive the trick; the gate opened and they entered straight in, trampled them down, and the masses broke. Their chieftain fled to Shijia'ang, and Lingjing Stockade was thereupon pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the jiashen year he marched on Lingjing and sent men to knock at the gate, pretending to deliver grain and fodder. The guards were taken in; the gate opened, his troops poured straight in and overran the place. The defenders scattered; their chieftain fled to Shijia'ang, and Lingjing Stockade was taken.

sentences.zh: 乙酉二月，清泉寨酋長王殼降，石家昂亦降。

translations.literal: In the second month of the yiyou year, the chieftain Wang Ke of Qingquan Stockade surrendered, and Shijia'ang also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the yiyou year the chieftain Wang Ke of Qingquan Stockade submitted, and Shijia'ang followed suit.

sentences.zh: 丁亥五月，姦人夜獻太原東門于武仙，仙引兵入，哈剌拔都鏖戰。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the dinghai year, traitors by night offered Taiyuan's eastern gate to Wu Xian; Xian led troops in and Halabatu fought fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the dinghai year traitors opened Taiyuan's eastern gate to Wu Xian by night. Xian led his army in, and Halabatu fought him tooth and nail.

sentences.zh: 仙兵大至，諸將自城外呼曰：「攸哈剌拔都，汝當出！

translations.literal: Xian's troops arrived in great numbers; the generals called from outside the walls: "You Halabatu, you should come out!
translations.idiomatic: When Xian's forces swelled, his generals shouted from beyond the walls: "You Halabatu—you must come out!"

sentences.zh: 」哈剌拔都曰：「真定史天倪，平陽李守忠，隰州田雄，皆失守矣，我又棄太原，將何面目見主上及國王乎！

translations.literal: Halabatu said: "Shi Tianni of Zhending, Li Shouzhong of Pingyang, and Tian Xiong of Xizhou have all lost their posts. If I too abandon Taiyuan, with what face shall I see the sovereign and the prince!
translations.idiomatic: Halabatu answered: "Shi Tianni lost Zhending, Li Shouzhong lost Pingyang, and Tian Xiong lost Xizhou. If I abandon Taiyuan as well, how could I face the sovereign or the prince?"

sentences.zh: 家屬任公等所俘，哈剌拔都誓與城同存亡。

translations.literal: His household had been captured by Ren Gong and others; Halabatu swore to live or die with the city.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been taken by Ren Gong and the rest, yet Halabatu swore to stand or fall with the city.

sentences.zh: 」遂歿于陣。

translations.literal: He thereupon died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He fell fighting on the field.

sentences.zh: 太祖以其子幼，命其表弟王七十復立太原。

translations.literal: The Founder, because his son was young, ordered his cousin Wang Qishi to re-establish Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Because his son was still a child, the Founder appointed his cousin Wang Qishi to restore order at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 己丑，攻鳳翔府，中砲死。

translations.literal: In the year jichou, attacking Fengxiang Prefecture, he was struck by artillery and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the jichou year, while assaulting Fengxiang Prefecture, he was killed by a cannon shot.

sentences.zh: 哈剌拔都長子忙兀台，嗣鎮太原。

translations.literal: Halabatu's eldest son Mangutai succeeded him in garrisoning Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Halabatu's eldest son Mangutai succeeded him as commander at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 任志，潞州人。

translations.literal: Ren Zhi was a man of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhi came from Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲戊寅，太師、國王木華黎略地至潞州，志首迎降，國王授以虎符，俾充元帥，收輯山寨。

translations.literal: In the year wuyin, the Grand Preceptor and Prince Muqali in reducing territory reached Luzhou; Zhi was the first to welcome and surrender. The prince gave him a tiger tally and appointed him marshal to gather in the mountain stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuyin year the Grand Preceptor and Prince Muqali reached Luzhou on campaign. Zhi was the first to submit, and the prince gave him a tiger tally, made him marshal, and charged him with bringing the mountain stockades to heel.

sentences.zh: 數與金兵戰，比有功。

translations.literal: He fought with Jin troops many times and each time had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the Jin again and again and distinguished himself each time.

sentences.zh: 金嘗擒其長子如山以招之，曰：「降則爾子得生，不降則死。

translations.literal: The Jin once captured his eldest son Rushan to entice him, saying: "If you surrender your son will live; if not he will die.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin once seized his eldest son Rushan to win him over, saying: "Surrender and your son lives; refuse and he dies."

sentences.zh: 」志曰：「我為大朝之帥，豈愛一子！

translations.literal: Zhi said: "I am marshal of the Great Dynasty—how could I cherish one son!
translations.idiomatic: Zhi replied: "I am marshal of the Great Dynasty—would I value one son above my duty!"

sentences.zh: 」親射其子殪之。

translations.literal: He personally shot his son and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He took up his bow and shot his son dead with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 木華黎嘗召諸將議事，志亦預徵，道經武安，其縣已反為金，志死之。

translations.literal: Muqali once summoned the generals to discuss affairs; Zhi was also summoned to attend. Passing through Wu'an, he found the county had already rebelled and returned to the Jin; Zhi died there.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali once summoned his generals for counsel, and Zhi was among those called. On the road through Wu'an he found the county had gone over to the Jin again, and there he met his death.

sentences.zh: 國王閔之，令其子存襲。

translations.literal: The prince mourned him and had his son Cun succeed to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The prince mourned him and appointed his son Cun to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 庚寅歲，金將武仙攻潞州，存戰死。

translations.literal: In the year gengyin, the Jin general Wu Xian attacked Luzhou and Cun died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengyin year the Jin general Wu Xian attacked Luzhou, and Cun fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 辛卯正月，有旨潞州元帥任存妻孥家屬，令有司廩給，仍賜第以居之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the xinmao year, an order was issued that the wife, children, and household of Luzhou Marshal Ren Cun were to be provisioned by the relevant offices and a residence was still to be bestowed for them to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the xinmao year an edict ordered that the wife, children, and household of Luzhou Marshal Ren Cun be maintained at public expense and that a residence be granted them.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以存父子死事，子立尚幼，先官其姪成為潞州長官，待立長而還授之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, because father and son Cun had died in service and the son Li was still young, his nephew Cheng was first appointed chief of Luzhou, to be returned to Li when Li grew up.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, because father and son had died in service and Li was still a child, his nephew Cheng was appointed chief of Luzhou until Li came of age, when the post would revert to him.

sentences.zh: 成卒，授立潞州長官，佩金符。

translations.literal: When Cheng died, Li was appointed chief of Luzhou and given a golden tally.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng died, Li was made chief of Luzhou and granted a golden tally.

sentences.zh: 後歷澤州尹，遷陳州，卒。

translations.literal: Later he served as prefect of Zezhou, was transferred to Chenzhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Zezhou, was transferred to Chenzhou, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 耶律忒末，契丹人。

translations.literal: Yelü Temei was a Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Temei was a Khitan.

sentences.zh: 父丑哥仕遼為都統，遼亡，不屈節，夫婦俱死焉。

translations.literal: His father Chouge served the Liao as commander-in-chief; when the Liao perished he would not bend his integrity, and husband and wife both died.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chouge had served the Liao as commander-in-chief. When the dynasty fell he refused to submit, and he and his wife both died rather than yield.

sentences.zh: 金主憫其忠義，授忒末都統。

translations.literal: The Jin ruler pitied their loyalty and righteousness and appointed Temei commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor, moved by their loyalty, made Temei commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 歲甲戌，國兵至，金徙于汴，忒末及子天祐率衆三萬內附，授帥府監軍，天祐招討使，從元帥史天倪略趙州平棘、欒城、元氏、柏鄉、贊皇、臨城等縣，籍其民五千餘，置吏安輯焉。

translations.literal: In the year jiaxu the state's army arrived; the Jin moved to Bian. Temei and his son Tianyou led thirty thousand men in internal submission and were appointed supervisor of the marshal's headquarters and pacification commissioner respectively. Following Marshal Shi Tianni they reduced Pingji, Luancheng, Yuanshi, Baixiang, Zanhuang, Lincheng, and other counties of Zhaozhou, registered more than five thousand of their people, and set up officials to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiaxu year the imperial armies arrived and the Jin court withdrew to Bian. Temei and his son Tianyou led thirty thousand men in submission. Temei was made supervisor of the marshal's headquarters and Tianyou pacification commissioner. They followed Marshal Shi Tianni in reducing Pingji, Luancheng, Yuanshi, Baixiang, Zanhuang, Lincheng, and other counties of Zhaozhou, registered more than five thousand households, and appointed officials to govern them.

sentences.zh: 歲辛巳，太師木華黎統領諸道兵馬，承制加忒末洺州等路征行元帥，與天祐略邢、洺、磁、相、懷、孟，昭花馬劉元帥，有功。

translations.literal: In the year xinsi, the Grand Preceptor Muqali commanded military forces of all circuits and, acting by commission, further appointed Temei campaigning marshal of the circuits including Mingzhou. With Tianyou he reduced Xing, Ming, Ci, Xiang, Huai, and Meng, joined Marshal Liu Zhaohuama, and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinsi year Grand Preceptor Muqali took command of the armies of all circuits and, acting under commission, promoted Temei to campaigning marshal of the Mingzhou circuit and allied commands. With Tianyou he campaigned through Xing, Ming, Ci, Xiang, Huai, and Meng alongside Marshal Liu Zhaohuama and won distinction.

sentences.zh: 木華黎又承制授忒末真定路安撫使、洺州元帥，進兵臨澤潞，降其民六千餘戶，以功遷河北西路安撫使，兼澤潞元帥府事。

translations.literal: Muqali again, acting by commission, appointed Temei pacification commissioner of the Zhending Circuit and marshal of Mingzhou; he advanced troops to approach Ze and Lu, received the submission of more than six thousand households, and for his merit was transferred to pacification commissioner of the Western Hebei Circuit, concurrently administering the Ze-Lu Marshal's Office.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali again commissioned him as pacification commissioner of the Zhending Circuit and marshal of Mingzhou. He advanced on Ze and Lu, received the submission of more than six thousand households, and for these services was promoted to pacification commissioner of the Western Hebei Circuit while also directing the Ze-Lu Marshal's Office.

sentences.zh: 壬午，致仕，退居真定。

translations.literal: In the year renwu he retired from office and withdrew to dwell at Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: In the renwu year he retired from office and withdrew to Zhending.

sentences.zh: 天祐襲職，從天倪攻取益都諸城，略滄、棣，得戶七千，兼滄、棣州達魯花赤，佩金符。

translations.literal: Tianyou inherited the office; following Tianni he attacked and took the various cities of Yidu, raided Cang and Di, obtained seven thousand households, concurrently served as darughachi of Cang and Di prefectures, and wore a golden tally.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou succeeded to his father's post. Following Shi Tianni, he captured the cities of Yidu, raided Cang and Di, and registered seven thousand households. He was appointed darughachi of Cang and Di prefectures and granted a golden tally.

sentences.zh: 時金鹽山衛鎮鹽場未下，天祐以計克之，歲運鹽四千席，以佐軍儲。

translations.literal: At the time the salt field of the Jin Yanshan guard town had not been taken; Tianyou by stratagem overcame it, annually transporting four thousand bundles of salt to assist military stores.
translations.idiomatic: The salt works at Yanshan, still held by the Jin, had not yet fallen. Tianyou took them by stratagem and thereafter shipped four thousand bundles of salt each year to supplement the army's provisions.

sentences.zh: 甲申，攻大名，拔之。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, he attacked Daming and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day he attacked Daming and captured it.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，金降將武仙據真定以叛，殺守將史天倪。

translations.literal: On yiyou, the Jin surrendered general Wu Xian seized Zhending in rebellion and killed the defending general Shi Tianni.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day the Jin defector Wu Xian rose in rebellion at Zhending and killed the garrison commander Shi Tianni.

sentences.zh: 忒末父子夜踰城而出，將以聞，會天倪弟天澤還自北京，遇諸滿城，合蒙古諸軍南與賊戰，走武仙，復真定。

translations.literal: Temei, father and son, at night climbed over the wall and went out, intending to report it; it happened that Tianni's younger brother Tianze was returning from Beiping, met them at Mancheng, combined with the Mongol armies and went south to battle the rebels, drove off Wu Xian, and recovered Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Temei and his son slipped over the wall by night to bring word of the rebellion. By chance Shi Tianni's brother Tianze was returning from Beiping; they met him at Mancheng, joined the Mongol forces, marched south against the rebels, put Wu Xian to flight, and recovered Zhending.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以天澤襲兄爵，而以天祐鎮趙州。

translations.literal: The court had Tianze inherit his elder brother's rank, and stationed Tianyou at Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted Tianze his elder brother's title and posted Tianyou as garrison commander at Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，仙復犯真定，天澤潛師出藁城，忒末與其妻石抹氏，及家孥在真定者，皆陷焉。

translations.literal: The next year Xian again invaded Zhending; Tianze moved troops secretly out of Gaocheng; Temei and his wife of the Shimou clan, and all kinfolk in Zhending, all fell into enemy hands.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wu Xian struck at Zhending again. Tianze slipped out of Gaocheng with a hidden force, but Temei, his wife Lady Shimou, and every member of their family still in Zhending were captured.

sentences.zh: 仙遣其僕劉攬兒，持書誘天祐曰：「汝能誅趙州官吏以降，當活汝父母，仍授汝元帥；

translations.literal: Xian sent his servant Liu Lan'er with a letter to entice Tianyou, saying: "If you can kill the officials of Zhaozhou and submit, your parents will be spared, and you will still be made marshal;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian sent his servant Liu Lan'er with a letter offering Tianyou a bargain: "Slay the officials of Zhaozhou and surrender, and I will spare your parents and make you marshal;

sentences.zh: 不爾，盡烹之。

translations.literal: If not, all will be boiled to death.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I will boil them all alive."

sentences.zh: 」忒末密令攬兒語天祐曰：「仙賊狡猾，汝所知也，毋以我故，墮其機阱，以虧忠節。

translations.literal: Temei secretly ordered Lan'er to tell Tianyou: "The bandit Xian is crafty—you know this—do not for my sake fall into his trap and impair your loyalty and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Temei secretly told Lan'er to say to Tianyou: "You know how cunning that rebel Wu Xian is. Do not on my account fall into his snare and betray your loyalty.

sentences.zh: 且忠孝難兩全，汝能固守，不失國家大計，我視刀鋸甘如蜜矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, loyalty and filial piety are hard to fulfill together; if you can hold firmly and not lose the great plan of the state, I regard knives and saws as sweet as honey.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty and filial piety cannot both be satisfied. If you hold the line and do not abandon the state's larger purpose, I shall welcome the executioner's blade as gladly as honey."

sentences.zh: 」天祐慟哭承命，馳至藁城，以賊書示天澤。

translations.literal: Tianyou wept bitterly and accepted the charge; he galloped to Gaocheng and showed the rebel's letter to Tianze.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou wept as he accepted his father's charge, rode hard to Gaocheng, and showed Wu Xian's letter to Tianze.

sentences.zh: 天澤曰：「王陵之事，照耀史冊，汝能遵父命，忠誠許國，功不在王陵下。

translations.literal: Tianze said: "Wang Ling's affair shines in the historical records; if you can follow your father's command, loyally devote yourself to the state, your merit will not fall below Wang Ling's.
translations.idiomatic: Tianze said: "Wang Ling's story still illumines the annals. Obey your father's charge, serve the state with your whole loyalty, and your merit will rival his.

sentences.zh: 」天祐乃趨還趙壁，率衆殊死戰，仙怒，盡殺忒末家一十八人。

translations.literal: Tianyou then hurried back to the walls of Zhao, led the multitude in a fight to the death; Xian in anger completely killed eighteen people of Temei's family.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou raced back to the defenses at Zhao and led his men in a desperate fight. Enraged, Wu Xian put all eighteen members of Temei's household to death.

sentences.zh: 戰于欒城、元氏、高邑、柏鄉，仙兵屢挫。

translations.literal: Battles were fought at Luancheng, Yuanshi, Gaoyi, and Baixiang; Xian's troops were repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They fought at Luancheng, Yuanshi, Gaoyi, and Baixiang, and Wu Xian's forces suffered defeat after defeat.

sentences.zh: 監軍張林密搆仙黨，啟關納賊。

translations.literal: The supervising officer Zhang Lin secretly colluded with Xian's faction, opened the gate, and admitted the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison supervisor Zhang Lin secretly plotted with Wu Xian's party, opened the gates, and let the rebels in.

sentences.zh: 天祐倉皇巷戰，手殺數十人，身被十餘瘡，斬關出，復收散卒圍城。

translations.literal: Tianyou in haste fought in the alleys, with his own hand killed several tens of men, his body received more than ten wounds, cut through the barrier and went out, again gathered scattered soldiers and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting through the streets in disarray, Tianyou slew dozens with his own hand and took more than ten wounds. He cut his way through the gate, rallied his scattered troops, and laid siege to the city again.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，賊棄城走，追至藁城，會天澤兵夾擊，殺林。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the rebels abandoned the city and fled; pursued to Gaocheng, they joined Tianze's troops in a pincer attack and killed Lin.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day the rebels abandoned the city and fled. Pursued to Gaocheng, they were caught between Tianyou's force and Tianze's army; Zhang Lin was killed.

sentences.zh: 加奉國上將軍、洺州征行元帥，兼趙州安撫使。

translations.literal: He was further made General Who Upholds the State, campaigning marshal of Mingzhou, and concurrently pacification commissioner of Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Upholds the State and campaigning marshal of Mingzhou, while retaining the post of pacification commissioner of Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 以傷憊致仕，居趙，卒。

translations.literal: Because of wounds and exhaustion he retired from office, dwelt at Zhao, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Worn out by his wounds, he retired from office, lived at Zhao, and died there.

sentences.zh: 孫世枻，朝列大夫、江西榷茶都轉運使。

translations.literal: His grandson Shiqi held the titles Court Rank Grandee and Director-General of Salt and Tea Transport of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Shiqi rose to Court Rank Grandee and Director-General of Salt and Tea Transport in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 伯八，晃合丹氏。

translations.literal: Bo Ba was of the Huanghedan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Ba belonged to the Huanghedan clan.

sentences.zh: 祖明里也赤哥，嘗隸太祖帳下。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mingalijichige once served under the Taizu within his personal following.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mingalijichige had once served in the Taizu's personal retinue.

sentences.zh: 初，怯列王可罕與太祖為鄰國，誓相親好，既而敗盟，與其子先髡潛謀，欲襲太祖，因遣使通問，許以女妻太祖弟合撒兒。

translations.literal: In the beginning the Kereyid Wang Khan was a neighboring state to the Taizu; they swore mutual friendship, but afterward he broke the covenant and with his son Senggum secretly plotted to strike the Taizu; therefore he sent envoys with greetings, promising to give his daughter in marriage to the Taizu's younger brother Hasar.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Kereyid Wang Khan was the Taizu's neighbor and ally by oath. When he broke faith, he and his son Senggum plotted in secret to ambush the Taizu. Wang Khan sent envoys bearing greetings and offered his daughter in marriage to the Taizu's brother Hasar.

sentences.zh: 至期，太祖欲往，明里也赤哥疑其詐，諫止之。

translations.literal: When the day came the Taizu wished to go; Mingalijichige suspected treachery and remonstrated to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: When the day arrived the Taizu meant to go. Mingalijichige suspected a trap and pleaded with him to stay away.

sentences.zh: 王可罕知謀泄，遂謀入寇，後為太祖所滅。

translations.literal: Wang Khan, knowing the plot had leaked, then plotted an incursion; afterward he was destroyed by the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Khan learned the plot had been exposed, he planned an invasion instead—and was eventually destroyed by the Taizu.

sentences.zh: 父脫倫闍里必，扈從太祖征西域，累立奇功。

translations.literal: His father Tuolunjilibi accompanied the Taizu in campaigning in the Western Regions and repeatedly achieved remarkable merit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tuolunjilibi followed the Taizu on the western campaigns and won repeated distinction.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，以伯八舊臣子孫，擢為萬戶，命領諸部軍馬屯守欠欠州。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, because Bo Ba was a descendant of an old minister, he was promoted to commander of ten thousand households and ordered to lead the armies of various tribes in garrison at Qianqian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai took the throne he raised Bo Ba, as the scion of an old servant family, to commander of ten thousand households and ordered him to garrison Qianqian Prefecture with troops from the affiliated tribes.

sentences.zh: 至元十二年，親王昔列吉、脫鐵木兒叛，奔海都。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan, the imperial prince Chiregui and Tuotiemur rebelled and fled to Kaidu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 12 the princes Chiregui and Tuotiemur rebelled and fled to Kaidu.

sentences.zh: 伯八以聞，且願提兵往討之，未得命，為彼所襲，死焉。

translations.literal: Bo Ba reported it and moreover wished to lead troops to go punish them; before he received orders, he was attacked by them and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Ba sent word to the court and volunteered to lead troops against them. Before orders came he was attacked by the rebels and killed.

sentences.zh: 脫鐵木兒虜其二子八剌、不蘭奚，分置左右，居歲餘，待之頗厚。

translations.literal: Tuotiemur captured his two sons Bala and Bulanxi, placed them on his left and right; after dwelling more than a year he treated them quite generously.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotiemur took Bo Ba's two sons, Bala and Bulanxi, as captives and kept them at his side. For more than a year he treated them with marked kindness.

sentences.zh: 八剌陰結脫鐵木兒近侍也里伯禿，謀報父仇，後為也伯里禿家人泄其謀。

translations.literal: Bala secretly joined with Tuotiemur's close attendant Yelibitu, plotting to avenge his father's death; afterward Yelibitu's household members exposed the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Bala won over Tuotiemur's attendant Yelibitu and plotted vengeance for his father. The scheme was betrayed by a member of Yelibitu's household.

sentences.zh: 八剌知事不成，將家族南奔，脫鐵木兒遣騎追之，至一河，八剌馬驚，不能渡，回拒之，射中數人，力窮，兄弟就擒。

translations.literal: Bala, knowing the affair would not succeed, was about to flee south with his clan; Tuotiemur sent riders in pursuit; reaching a river, Bala's horse was startled and could not cross; turning back he resisted, hit several men with arrows; strength exhausted, the brothers were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Realizing the plot had failed, Bala fled south with his family. Tuotiemur sent horsemen in pursuit. At a river Bala's mount panicked and could not cross. He turned back, held the pursuers off with his bow, and brought down several men before, spent at last, he and his brother were taken.

sentences.zh: 脫鐵木兒責之曰：「我待汝厚甚，而汝反為此耶！

translations.literal: Tuotiemur rebuked them, saying: "I treated you very generously—yet you turn around and do this!
translations.idiomatic: Tuotiemur upbraided him: "I treated you with great kindness—yet you repay me with treachery!

sentences.zh: 」八剌曰：「汝背叛君上，害我父，掠我親屬，我誓欲殺汝，以報君父之讎，今力窮被執，從汝所為！

translations.literal: Bala said: "You betrayed your sovereign, harmed my father, plundered my kin—I vowed to kill you to repay the feud of sovereign and father; now strength exhausted and captured, do as you will!
translations.idiomatic: Bala answered: "You rebelled against your lord, killed my father, and seized my kin. I swore to kill you and avenge my sovereign and my father. My strength is spent and I am your prisoner—do what you will!

sentences.zh: 」逼令跪，不屈，以鐵撾碎其膝，終不跪，與弟不闌奚同被害。

translations.literal: He was forced to kneel but would not submit; with an iron mace his knees were shattered; to the end he would not kneel; he and his younger brother Bulanxi were alike killed.
translations.idiomatic: They forced him to kneel, but he refused. They crushed his knees with iron maces, yet he still would not kneel. He and his brother Bulanxi were killed together.

sentences.zh: 幼子何都兀赤，官至河北河南道肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: The youngest son Heduwuchi reached the office of surveillance commissioner of the Hebei-Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Ba's youngest son, Heduwuchi, rose to surveillance commissioner of the Hebei-Henan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 合剌普華，岳璘帖木爾子也。

translations.literal: Heilapuhua was the son of Yuelintiemuer.
translations.idiomatic: Heilapuhua was a son of Yuelintiemuer.

sentences.zh: 幼侍母奧敦氏居益都，嘗歎曰：「幼而不學，有不墮吾宗者乎！

translations.literal: In youth he attended his mother Lady Audun and dwelt at Yidu; he once sighed and said: "Young and not studying—is there one who will not bring down our clan!
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he lived with his mother Lady Audun at Yidu and once sighed: "A child who does not study—will he not bring ruin on our house?

sentences.zh: 」父時以斷事官建牙保定，合剌普華往白其志。

translations.literal: At the time his father was establishing his headquarters at Baoding as a judicial officer; Heilapuhua went to declare his intent.
translations.idiomatic: His father was then serving as a judicial officer at Baoding, and Heilapuhua went to tell him of his resolve.

sentences.zh: 父奇之，俾習畏兀書及經史，記誦精敏，出於天性。

translations.literal: His father marveled at this and had him study Uighur script and the classics and histories; he was keen in memorizing and reciting, arising from inborn nature.
translations.idiomatic: His father was impressed and set him to learn Uighur script and the classics and histories. He memorized with quick intelligence that seemed inborn.

sentences.zh: 李璮畔，其母攜季子脫烈普華避地登、萊間，音問隔絕，號泣徹晝夜。

translations.literal: When Li Tan rebelled, his mother carried his youngest brother Tuoliepuhua to take refuge between Deng and Lai; letters and inquiries were cut off, and he wept and wailed through day and night.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Tan rebelled, his mother fled with her youngest son Tuoliepuhua to the coast between Deng and Lai. Cut off from all word of them, Heilapuhua wept day and night.

sentences.zh: 繼從從叔父撒吉思平賊山東，卒奉其母以歸。

translations.literal: Thereafter he followed his father's younger cousin Sagis and pacified the rebels in Shandong; at last he brought his mother back in return.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined his grand-uncle Sagis in pacifying the rebellion in Shandong and finally brought his mother home.

sentences.zh: 撒吉思深加器重，自謂其才不及，言於世祖，召給宿衛。

translations.literal: Sagis greatly valued him, saying himself that his talent did not reach his level, spoke of him to Shizu, who summoned him to serve in the imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sagis thought highly of him, confessing that he could not match the younger man's gifts, and recommended him to Kublai, who summoned him into the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 嘗以事至益都，於四腳山下置廣興、商山二冶，以勞授金符，為商山鐵冶都提舉；

translations.literal: Once on business he reached Yidu; at the foot of Mount Sijiao he established two smelters, Guangxing and Shangshan; for his labors he was given a golden tally as Director-General of the Shangshan Iron Smeltery;
translations.idiomatic: When business took him to Yidu, he founded two ironworks, Guangxing and Shangshan, at the foot of Mount Sijiao. For these services he received a golden tally and was made director-general of the Shangshan smeltery;

sentences.zh: 未及代，以職讓其弟。

translations.literal: Before his term of replacement came he yielded the office to his younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Before his tour of duty ended he resigned the post in favor of his younger brother.

sentences.zh: 時兵南伐，餽運繁興，被選為行都漕運使，帥諸翼兵萬五千人，從事飛輓。

translations.literal: At the time troops were campaigning south and transport of supplies was greatly pressed; he was selected as acting director of the capital grain transport, commanding fifteen thousand auxiliary troops to engage in rapid transport.
translations.idiomatic: While the armies marched south and grain transport grew urgent, he was chosen acting director of capital grain transport. He commanded fifteen thousand auxiliary troops in emergency convoy duty.

sentences.zh: 江南平，上疏言：「親肺腑，禮大臣，以存國家之體。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, he memorialized, saying: "Cherish kin of flesh and bone, treat great ministers with ceremony, to preserve the body's form of the state.
translations.idiomatic: After the south was pacified he submitted a memorial: "Honor those nearest the throne in blood, treat great ministers with due ceremony, and so preserve the dignity of the state.

sentences.zh: 興學校，獎名節，以勵天下之士。

translations.literal: Raise up schools, reward integrity and reputation, to encourage the scholars of all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Establish schools and reward men of principle, so as to stir the scholars of the realm.

sentences.zh: 正名分，嚴考課，以定百官之法。

translations.literal: Rectify names and ranks, strictly conduct examinations and assessments, to fix the law for the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Clarify ranks and titles, tighten performance review, and fix the standards by which officials are judged.

sentences.zh: 通泉幣，却貢獻，以厚生民之本。

translations.literal: Circulate currency, reject tribute offerings, to thicken the foundation of the people's livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Keep currency in circulation, refuse excessive tribute, and strengthen the people's material foundation.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「江南新附，宜招舊族，力穡通商，弛征薄入，以撫馴其民，不然，恐尚煩宵旰之慮。

translations.literal: He also said: "Jiangnan has newly submitted; it is fitting to summon the old clans, labor in farming and open trade, relax levies and lighten collections, to soothe and tame its people; otherwise, I fear it will still trouble the sovereign's sleepless cares.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "The newly submitted south should have its old gentry recalled to land and trade, with lighter taxes and easier levies, so the people may be reassured. Otherwise Your Majesty may yet lie awake over the region.

sentences.zh: 」帝多采用其言。

translations.literal: The emperor largely adopted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted most of his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 屬漕米二十萬，繇邗溝達于河，舟覆，損十之一，而又每斛視都斛虧三升。

translations.literal: He was charged with two hundred thousand piculs of transported grain, conveyed by the Hangou Canal to reach the river; boats capsized and one tenth was lost; moreover each picul measured against the capital standard was short by three sheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was responsible for transporting two hundred thousand piculs of grain along the Hangou Canal to the Yellow River. Boats foundered and a tenth of the grain was lost; each picul moreover measured three sheng short against the capital standard.

sentences.zh: 時阿合馬專政，責償舟人。

translations.literal: At the time Ahmad monopolized government and demanded repayment from the boatmen.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad then held sole power and demanded that the boatmen make good the loss.

sentences.zh: 合剌普華伏闕抗言：「量之踦贏，出於元降，而水道之虞，非人力所及。

translations.literal: Heilapuhua prostrated himself at the palace gate and spoke up: "Shortage and surplus in measuring arise from the original shortfall, while perils of the water route are not within human reach.
translations.idiomatic: Heilapuhua prostrated himself before the palace and protested: "Short weight comes from the original shortage in the grain itself, and losses on the waterways are beyond human control.

sentences.zh: 且彼雖罄其家，不足以償，苟朝廷必不任虧損，臣獨當其辜。

translations.literal: Moreover, though they exhaust their households it is not enough to repay; if the court surely will not allow loss, I alone will bear the guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the boatmen sold all they owned they could not repay it. If the court will tolerate no loss, let me alone bear the penalty.

sentences.zh: 」詔勿治。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that the matter not be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict came down forbidding prosecution.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬憤之，乃出合剌普華為寧海路達魯花赤，後遷江西宣慰使，未至官，改廣東都轉運鹽使，兼領諸番市舶。

translations.literal: Ahmad resented this and therefore sent Heilapuhua out as darughachi of the Ninghai Circuit; later transferred as relief commissioner of Jiangxi—before he reached his post, changed to director-general of salt transport of Guangdong, concurrently overseeing the maritime trade of all foreign merchant fleets.
translations.idiomatic: Smarting from the rebuff, Ahmad posted Heilapuhua to Ninghai Circuit as darughachi. He was later appointed Jiangxi relief commissioner, but before he took up that office he was shifted to Director-General of Salt Transport in Guangdong, with oversight of foreign trade as well.

sentences.zh: 時盜梗鹽法，陳良臣扇東莞、香山、惠州負販之徒萬人為亂，江西行省命與招討使荅失蠻討捕之，先驅斬渠魁，以訊馘告，躬抵賊巢，招誘餘黨復業，仍條言鹽法之不便者，悉除其害。

translations.literal: At the time bandits obstructed the salt laws; Chen Liangchen incited ten thousand porters and peddlers of Dongguan, Xiangshan, and Huizhou into rebellion; the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat ordered him together with the pacification commissioner Dashiman to suppress and capture them; he first advanced, beheaded the ringleaders, reported with interrogation records and severed heads; personally reached the bandits' lair, enticed remaining followers to return to their occupations, and moreover listed articulations of inconveniences in the salt laws, entirely removing their harms.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were disrupting the salt monopoly when Chen Liangchen rallied ten thousand peddlers from Dongguan, Xiangshan, and Huizhou in revolt. The Jiangxi Branch Secretariat ordered Heilapuhua, together with the pacification commissioner Dashiman, to suppress them. He rode ahead, cut down the ringleaders, and sent back their heads with his report. He went in person to the rebels' stronghold, persuaded the remnants to resume honest livelihoods, and drafted a list of abuses in the salt regulations, which were then abolished.

sentences.zh: 按察使脫歡大為姦利，遂奏罷之。

translations.literal: The surveillance commissioner Tuo Huan greatly committed illicit profit; he therefore memorialized to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: The surveillance commissioner Tuo Huan had enriched himself by gross corruption; Heilapuhua memorialized for his removal and the court dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 群盜歐南喜僭王號，偽署丞相、招討，衆號十萬。

translations.literal: The bandit Ou Nanxi usurped a royal title, falsely appointed chancellors and pacification commissioners, and his multitude was called one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The outlaw Ou Nanxi declared himself king, set up a shadow government with chancellors and pacification commissioners, and claimed a force of one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 因圖上其山川形勢，及攻取之策三十餘條，遂與都元帥課兒伯海牙、宣慰都元帥白佐、萬戶王守信等，分兵搤之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he mapped and submitted the terrain and its features, together with more than thirty articles of strategies for attack and capture; then with the commander-in-chief Kuo'er Bohaiya, relief commander-in-chief Bai Zuo, commander of ten thousand households Wang Shouxin, and others, he divided troops to block them.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted maps of the local terrain with more than thirty proposed battle plans, then joined Commander-in-Chief Kuo'er Bohaiya, Relief Commander-in-Chief Bai Zuo, the commander of ten thousand households Wang Shouxin, and others in dividing their forces to contain the rebels.

sentences.zh: 未幾，右丞唆都督兵征占城、交阯，屬護餉道。

translations.literal: Before long the right chancellor Suo Du commanded troops on the campaign against Champa and Jiaozhi; he was assigned to protect the supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, the right chancellor Suo Du marched against Champa and Annam, and Heilapuhua was assigned to guard the supply lines.

sentences.zh: 比至東莞、博羅二界中，遇劇賊歐、鍾等，橫絕石灣，其鋒銳甚。

translations.literal: When he reached the border between Dongguan and Boluo he met fierce bandits Ou, Zhong, and others, who blocked Shiwang transversely; their edge was very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: On the march through the borderlands of Dongguan and Boluo he encountered the fierce rebel Ou and Zhong, who barred the crossing at Shiwang with a very sharp attack.

sentences.zh: 合剌普華身先士卒，且戰且行，矢竭馬創，徒步格鬪，殺數十人，勇氣益厲，以衆寡不敵，為所執。

translations.literal: Heilapuhua himself led soldiers at the front; fighting as he went, his arrows were exhausted and his horse wounded; on foot he grappled in combat, killed several tens of men, his courage growing fiercer; because the many and few were unmatched he was captured by them.
translations.idiomatic: Heilapuhua fought in the van, advancing battle by battle until his arrows were spent and his horse wounded. On foot he closed with the enemy, killed dozens, and fought with mounting fury until, outnumbered, he was taken.

sentences.zh: 賊欲奉之為主，不屈，遂遇害于中心岡。

translations.literal: The bandits wished to make him their leader; he would not submit and was therefore killed at Zhongxing Gang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels tried to make him their leader. He refused and was killed at Zhongxing Ridge.

sentences.zh: 是夕，其妻希台特勒氏，夢其來告曰：「吾死矣。

translations.literal: That same evening his wife Lady Xitaitele dreamed he came to tell her: "I am dead.
translations.idiomatic: That very night his wife Lady Xitaitele dreamed that he came to her and said, "I am dead.

sentences.zh: 」知事張德、劉閏亦夢之，二人相繼死。

translations.literal: The prefectural aides Zhang De and Liu Run also dreamed of him; the two men successively died.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural aides Zhang De and Liu Run dreamed of him as well, and both men died soon after.

sentences.zh: 而軍中往往見其乘騅督戰云。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the army many often saw him riding a gelding and supervising battle, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers in the camp, it was said, often saw him riding a roan horse and directing the fight.

sentences.zh: 後贈戶部尚書、守忠全節功臣，諡忠愍。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously granted Minister of Revenue and the title of Merit Holder in Guarding Loyalty and Complete Integrity; his posthumous name was Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously made Minister of Revenue and Honored as a Merit Holder in Guarding Loyalty and Preserving Integrity, with the posthumous name Zhongmin ("Loyal and Lamented").

sentences.zh: 子二人：偰文質，越倫質。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Xiewenzhi and Yuelunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Xiewenzhi and Yuelunzhi.

sentences.zh: 偰文質官至吉安路達魯花赤，贈宣惠安遠功臣、禮部尚書，追封雲中郡侯，謚忠襄。

translations.literal: Xiewenzhi reached the office of darughachi of Ji'an Circuit; posthumously granted the title of Merit Holder in Proclaiming Kindness and Pacifying the Distant, Minister of Rites; posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Yunzhong; posthumous name Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiewenzhi became darughachi of Ji'an Circuit. After his death he was honored as Merit Holder in Proclaiming Kindness and Pacifying the Distant, Minister of Rites, and Marquis of Yunzhong, with the posthumous name Zhongxiang.

sentences.zh: 子六人，偰玉立、偰直堅、偰哲篤、偰朝吾、偰列箎，皆第進士。

translations.literal: Six sons—Xieyuli, Xiezhijian, Xiezhedu, Xiechaowu, and Xieliechi—all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons—Xieyuli, Xiezhijian, Xiezhedu, Xiechaowu, and Xieliechi—who all earned jinshi degrees.

sentences.zh: 偰哲篤官至江西行省右丞，以文學政事稱于時。

translations.literal: Xiezhedu reached the office of right chancellor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and was acclaimed in his time for literary and administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhedu rose to right chancellor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat and was celebrated in his day for his literary and administrative gifts.

sentences.zh: 越倫質子善著，偰哲篤子偰百僚遜，善著子正宗、阿兒思蘭，皆相繼登第。

translations.literal: Yuelunzhi's son Shanzhao, Xiezhedu's son Xiebailiaosun, Shanzhao's sons Zhengzong and A'ersilan—all in succession passed the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Yuelunzhi's son Shanzhao, Xiezhedu's son Xiebailiaosun, and Shanzhao's sons Zhengzong and A'ersilan all passed the examinations in successive generations.

sentences.zh: 一門世科之盛，當時所希有，君子蓋以為其忠義之報云。

translations.literal: The flourishing of examination degrees in one clan was rare in the age; gentlemen perhaps regarded it as the reward for his loyalty and righteousness, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Such a run of degrees in a single family was rare even then; men of discernment took it as Heaven's reward for Heilapuhua's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 劉天孚字裕民，大名人。

translations.literal: Liu Tianfu, style name Yumin, was a native of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tianfu, whose style was Yumin, came from Daming.

sentences.zh: 由中書譯史為東平緫管府判官，改都漕運司判官，知冠州，再知許州，所至有治績。

translations.literal: From a translation clerk of the Secretariat he became vice-prefect of the Dongping General Administration Office; changed to vice-director of the Capital Grain Transport Office; served as prefect of Guanzhou; served again as prefect of Xuzhou; wherever he went there was merit in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a clerk-translator in the Secretariat, he became vice-prefect of Dongping, then vice-director of the Capital Grain Transport Office, and served as prefect first of Guan and then of Xu, earning a record of sound administration wherever he was posted.

sentences.zh: 時檢核屯田，臨潁鄧艾口民稻田三百頃，有欲害之者，指為古屯，陳于中書，請復築之。

translations.literal: At the time when military colonies were being inspected, three hundred qing of civilian rice fields at Deng'aikou in Linying—someone wishing to harm them pointed to them as an ancient colony, memorialized the Secretariat, and asked to restore and build it up.
translations.idiomatic: During an inspection of military colony lands, someone tried to seize three hundred qing of farmland at Deng'aikou in Linying by claiming it as an old imperial estate and petitioned the Secretariat to have it reallocated.

sentences.zh: 中書下天孚按實，天孚為辨其非，章數上，乃止。

translations.literal: The Secretariat sent down to Tianfu to verify on the spot; Tianfu argued on its behalf that this was not so; memorial after memorial he submitted, and at last it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat assigned Tianfu to investigate. He proved the claim false and filed repeated memorials until the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 襄城與葉縣接壤，其南為湛河，襄城民食滄鹽，葉縣民食解鹽，刻石河南岸以為界。

translations.literal: Xiangcheng and Ye County bordered each other; to the south was the Zhan River; the people of Xiangcheng ate Cang salt, the people of Ye County ate Jie salt; they carved a stone on the south bank of the river as a boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangcheng and Ye County shared a border along the Zhan River to the south. Xiangcheng households used Cangzhou salt and Ye households used Jiezhou salt; a boundary stone was set on the river's south bank.

sentences.zh: 葉縣令有貪污者，妄徙石於北二里，誣其民食私鹽，繫治百餘家。

translations.literal: A magistrate of Ye County who was corrupt falsely moved the stone north two li, falsely accused its people of consuming private salt, and imprisoned and tried more than one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: A corrupt magistrate of Ye shifted the stone two li north, accused Xiangcheng folk of buying illicit salt, and imprisoned more than a hundred families.

sentences.zh: 兩縣鬪辯，葉縣倚陝漕勢以凌襄城。

translations.literal: The two counties disputed in argument; Ye County relied on the power of the Shaanxi grain transport to bully Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The counties wrangled before the authorities, and Ye leaned on the Shaanxi grain transport office to bully Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 中書遣官察其實，天孚為考其元界，移石故處，而葉縣令被罪去。

translations.literal: The Secretariat sent an official to investigate the truth; Tianfu examined the original boundary for them, moved the stone back to its old place, and the magistrate of Ye County was punished and removed.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat sent an investigator; Tianfu traced the original boundary, restored the marker stone, and the Ye magistrate was punished and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 歲大旱，天孚禱即雨。

translations.literal: In a year of great drought, Tianfu prayed and rain immediately came.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of severe drought Tianfu prayed, and rain fell at once.

sentences.zh: 野有蝗，天孚令民出捕，俄群烏來，啄蝗為盡。

translations.literal: In the fields there were locusts; Tianfu ordered the people to go out to catch them; soon flocks of crows came and pecked the locusts until none remained.
translations.idiomatic: When locusts plagued the fields he ordered the people out to destroy them; soon flocks of crows arrived and devoured the swarm.

sentences.zh: 明年麥熟時，有青蟲如蟊，食麥，人無可奈何，忽生大華蟲，盡嚼之。

translations.literal: The next year when wheat ripened there were green insects like blight that ate the wheat; people had no way to deal with them; suddenly large patterned insects were born and chewed them all up.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, as the wheat ripened, green vermin like blight devoured the crop until men could do nothing—then great spotted beetles appeared and ate the pests clean.

sentences.zh: 許人立碑頌焉。

translations.literal: The people of Xu erected a stele in praise thereof.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xu erected a stele in his praise.

sentences.zh: 轉萬億寶源庫同提舉，遷江西行省左右司郎中，以母老不赴。

translations.literal: Transferred as associate director of the Wan'yi Baoyuan Treasury; promoted to director in the left and right secretariats of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat—because his mother was old he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to associate director of the Wan'yi Baoyuan Treasury and then to director in the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat's left and right offices, but declined the latter appointment because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 俄丁母憂。

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，起知河中府，視事始兩月，陝西行省丞相阿思罕為亂，舉兵至河中。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was raised to serve as prefect of Hezhong Prefecture; he had governed only two months when the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat chancellor Asihan rebelled and raised troops to reach Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was appointed prefect of Hezhong. He had been in office barely two months when Asihan, chancellor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, rose in rebellion and marched on the city.

sentences.zh: 時事起不虞，達魯花赤朶兒只趨晉寧告亂，天孚日夜治戰守具，選丁壯，分守要害。

translations.literal: At the time the matter arose unexpectedly; the darughachi Duo'erzhi hurried to Jinning to report the rebellion; Tianfu day and night prepared implements for fighting and defense, selected able-bodied men, and divided them to guard strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: The revolt came without warning. The darughachi Duo'erzhi raced to Jinning to raise the alarm while Tianfu worked day and night preparing defenses, mustering strong men, and posting them at critical points.

sentences.zh: 令河東縣達魯花赤脫因都守大慶關津口，盡收船舫東岸。

translations.literal: He ordered the darughachi of Hedong County, Tuoyindu, to guard the pass at Daqing and collect all boats and ships on the east bank.
translations.idiomatic: He posted the Hedong County darughachi Tuoyindu at the Daqing pass to hold the crossing and had every vessel on the east bank seized.

sentences.zh: 令判官孫伯帖木兒守汾陰，推官程謙守禹門，河東縣尹王文義守風陵等渡。

translations.literal: He ordered the vice-prefect Sun Botiemuer to guard Fenyin, the investigating official Cheng Qian to guard Yumeng, and the magistrate of Hedong County Wang Weny to guard the crossings at Fengling and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He assigned Vice-Prefect Sun Botiemuer to Fenyin, Investigating Official Cheng Qian to Yumeng, and Hedong County Magistrate Wang Weny to the crossings at Fengling and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 阿思罕軍列柵河西岸，使來索舟，天孚度不能拒，凡八遣人至晉寧乞援兵，不報。

translations.literal: Asihan's army lined palisades on the west bank of the river; envoys came to demand boats; Tianfu judged he could not refuse; eight times in all he sent men to Jinning to beg for relief troops—no reply.
