translations.idiomatic: Asihan's army lined the west bank with palisades and sent envoys demanding boats. Seeing he could not hold them off, Tianfu eight times dispatched messengers to Jinning pleading for reinforcements—and received no answer.

sentences.zh: 居七日，阿思罕縛筏河上，欲縱火屠城，同知府事鐵哥，與河東廉訪副使明安荅見事急，且患城中人偪，乃詣阿思罕軍，阿思罕囚之，而斂船濟兵。

translations.literal: After seven days Asihan bound rafts on the river, intending to set fires and slaughter the city; the associate prefect Tiege and the Hedong assistant surveillance commissioner Ming'anda, seeing matters urgent and also fearing coercion from the people within the city, thereupon went to Asihan's army; Asihan imprisoned them and gathered boats to ferry troops across.
translations.idiomatic: After seven days Asihan lashed rafts on the river and prepared to burn the city and put it to the sword. Associate Prefect Tiege and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Ming'anda of Hedong, seeing the crisis and fearing pressure from the townspeople, went to Asihan's camp. Asihan imprisoned them, collected the boats, and crossed his army over.

sentences.zh: 兵既入城，阿思罕以扼河渡、鎖舟楫為天孚罪，欲脅使附己。

translations.literal: Once the troops had entered the city, Asihan made blocking the river crossing and locking up boats Tianfu's crime and wished to coerce him into joining himself.
translations.idiomatic: Once his troops were inside the city, Asihan accused Tianfu of blocking the crossing and seizing the boats and tried to force him to submit.

sentences.zh: 方坐府治，號令諸軍，天孚佩刀直前，衆遏之，不得進。

translations.literal: Just as he sat in the prefectural office issuing commands to the armies, Tianfu with drawn sword went straight forward; the crowd blocked him and he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Asihan sat in the prefectural hall issuing orders to his troops; Tianfu drew his sword and advanced—but the crowd held him back and he could not reach him.

sentences.zh: 退謂幕僚王從善等曰：「吾家本微賤，荷朝命至此，今不幸遭大變，吾何忍從之，而負上恩哉！

translations.literal: Withdrawing he said to his staff Wang Congshan and others: "My family was originally humble and low; I received the court's commission to reach this place; now unhappily meeting great calamity—how can I bear to follow him and betray the sovereign's favor!
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew and said to his staff Wang Congshan and the others: "My family was humble before the court raised me to this post. Now disaster has come upon us—how can I follow a rebel and betray the emperor's grace?

sentences.zh: 且與其辱於阿思罕之手，吾寧蹈河以死。

translations.literal: Rather than suffer disgrace at Asihan's hands, I would sooner throw myself into the river and die.
translations.idiomatic: Better to drown in the river than endure shame at Asihan's hands.

sentences.zh: 」遂拂衣出。

translations.literal: He thereupon shook out his robes and went out.
translations.idiomatic: With that he flung aside his robe and strode out.

sentences.zh: 時天寒，河冰方堅，天孚拔所佩刀斫冰開，北望為國語若祝謝者，再拜已，脫衣帽岸滸，乃投水中。

translations.literal: The weather was cold and the river ice had just hardened. Tianfu drew the sword at his belt and hacked the ice open, looked north and in the state language uttered words like prayer and thanks, bowed twice, removed his hat and robe on the bank, and cast himself into the water.
translations.idiomatic: The air was bitter cold and the river had frozen hard. Tianfu drew his sword and broke a path through the ice, turned north and murmured a blessing in Mongolian, bowed twice, stripped off his hat and cloak on the shore, and plunged into the current.

sentences.zh: 阿思罕大怒，籍其家。

translations.literal: Asihan was greatly enraged and confiscated his household property.
translations.idiomatic: Asihan flew into a rage and seized his family's property.

sentences.zh: 郡人咸哀痛之。

translations.literal: All the people of the prefecture mourned him in grief.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the prefecture grieved for him as one.

sentences.zh: 事平，詔其弟天惠，給驛以歸其柩，葬于大名。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, an edict was issued to his younger brother Tianhui to provide post-horses to bring back his coffin and bury him at Daming.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, the court ordered his younger brother Tianhui to use the courier service to bring home his coffin and bury him at Daming.

sentences.zh: 贈推誠秉節功臣、中奉大夫、河東山西道宣慰使、護軍、彭城郡侯，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Merit Holder in Sincere Devotion and Upholding Integrity, Palace Attendant Grand Master, pacification commissioner of the Hedong and Shanxi Circuit, protector of the army, and Marquis of Pengcheng Commandery, with the posthumous name Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Merit Holder in Sincere Devotion and Upholding Integrity, Palace Attendant Grand Master, pacification commissioner of the Hedong and Shanxi Circuit, protector of the army, and Marquis of Pengcheng, with the posthumous name Zhongyi, "Loyal and Resolute."

sentences.zh: 蕭景茂，漳州龍溪人也。

translations.literal: Xiao Jingmao was a man of Longxi in Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Jingmao came from Longxi in Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 性剛直孝友。

translations.literal: His nature was stern, upright, filial, and brotherly.
translations.idiomatic: He was stern, upright, and devoted to family.

sentences.zh: 家貧力農。

translations.literal: His family was poor and he labored at farming.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor, and he worked the fields with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 重改至元四年，南勝縣民李智甫作亂，掠龍溪。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Zhigai era under the Yuan, Li Zhifu, a man of Nansheng County, rose in rebellion and plundered Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Zhigai era, Li Zhifu of Nansheng County rebelled and raided Longxi.

sentences.zh: 景茂與兄佑集鄉丁拒之，據觀音山橋險，與賊戰。

translations.literal: Jingmao and his elder brother You gathered village militia to resist them, held the perilous ground at Guanyin Mountain Bridge, and fought the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmao and his elder brother You rallied the village militia, seized the choke point at Guanyin Mountain Bridge, and gave battle to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 衆敗，景茂被執。

translations.literal: The force was defeated and Jingmao was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Their force was broken, and Jingmao was taken.

sentences.zh: 賊脅使從己，景茂罵曰：「狗盜！

translations.literal: The bandits threatened him to follow them; Jingmao cursed, saying: "Dog thieves!
translations.idiomatic: The rebels tried to force him to join them. Jingmao spat back: "Cur dogs!

sentences.zh: 我生為大元民，死作隔洲鬼，豈從汝為逆耶！

translations.literal: I was born a subject of the Great Yuan; in death I shall be a ghost of Gezhou—how could I follow you in rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: I was born a subject of the Great Yuan; in death I shall be a ghost of Gezhou—would I follow you in treason!

sentences.zh: 」隔洲，其所居里也。

translations.literal: Gezhou was the name of the village where he dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: Gezhou was the name of his home village.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，縛景茂於樹，臠其肉，使自啖。

translations.literal: The bandits grew angry, bound Jingmao to a tree, sliced his flesh, and made him eat it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the rebels bound him to a tree, carved strips from his flesh, and forced him to eat them.

sentences.zh: 景茂益憤罵，賊遂以刀決其口，至耳傍，景茂罵不絕聲而死。

translations.literal: Jingmao cursed all the more in fury; the bandits thereupon used a knife to cut open his mouth as far as beside his ear; Jingmao died still cursing without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmao only cursed the louder. The rebels slashed his mouth open with a knife, cutting nearly to his ear, yet he died still shouting defiance.

sentences.zh: 有司上其事，朝廷命褒表之，仍給錢以葬。

translations.literal: The relevant offices reported the matter upward; the court ordered him commended and honored with a tablet, and moreover granted money for burial.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported his case to the court, which ordered him honored with a commemorative tablet and provided funds for his burial.
